papers.title: A Mathematical Model on the Resolution of Extrusion Bioprinting for the Development of New Bioinks
papers.abstract: Pneumatic extrusion-based bioprinting is a recent and interesting technology that is very useful for biomedical applications. However, many process parameters in the bioprinter need to be fully understood in order to print at an adequate resolution. In this paper, a simple yet accurate mathematical model to predict the printed width of a continuous hydrogel line is proposed, in which the resolution is expressed as a function of nozzle size, pressure, and printing speed. A thermo-responsive hydrogel, pluronic F127, is used to validate the model predictions. This model could provide a platform for future correlation studies on pneumatic extrusion-based bioprinting as well as for developing new bioink formulations.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了挤出式生物打印分辨率的数学模型，但未涉及AI/ML方法，与用户对AI集成生物打印的研究方向不直接相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate any AI or machine learning technique into the bioprinting workflow; it only provides a non-AI mathematical model for resolution prediction.

summary_zh.motivation: 建立预测挤出式生物打印线宽的数学模型，以指导生物墨水开发
summary_zh.method: 基于喷嘴尺寸、压力和打印速度，提出打印线宽预测公式
summary_zh.result: 模型预测与实验测量吻合，为生物墨水流变设计提供参考
summary_zh.validation: 通过打印Pluronic F127水凝胶线并测量宽度验证模型

summary_en.motivation: To develop a predictive mathematical model for extruded line width in bioprinting to guide bioink formulation.
summary_en.method: A simple analytical model expressing printed line width as a function of nozzle diameter, applied pressure, and printing speed.
summary_en.result: The model predictions closely match experimental measurements using Pluronic F127 hydrogel.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation by printing continuous hydrogel lines and comparing measured widths with model predictions.

papers.title: Bilateral total hip arthroplasty in femoral head avascular necrosis: functional outcomes and complications
papers.abstract: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is one of the successful and cost-benefit surgical treatments. One-stage bilateral THA (BTHA) offers many benefits. However, there are concerns about the safety of the procedure and higher complications. We aimed to evaluate the complications and outcomes of one-stage BTHA with Hardinge approach for femoral head avascular necrosis patients. A total of 60 patients from April 2009 and May 2013, were underwent one-stage bilateral total hip arthroplasty (BTHA) in Milad and Erfan hospitals, Tehran, Iran. A prospective analysis of the functional outcomes and complications of one-stage BTHA through Hardinge approach in patients with femoral head avascular necrosis (AVN) performed. We evaluated all patients clinically and radiologically with serial follow-ups. A clinical hip score based upon the modified Harris Hip Score (MHHS) was performed preoperatively and again postoperatively. During period of study 44 men (73.3%) and 16 women (26.6%) with a mean age of 31.40±4.08 years (range 25 to 36 years) at the time of presentation were entered. The mean surgical time was 2.6±0.38 hrs. The mean hospital stay was 3.50±0.72 days. Hemoglobin level decreased significantly after operation (P= 0.046). There was no reported patient with perioperative death, deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, infection, dislocation, periprosthetic fracture or heterotrophic ossification. The mean preoperative MHHS score was 47.93±7.33 in patients. MHHS score improved to 95.06±3.47 in the last follow-up (P=0.0001).Our results recommend the use of one-stage BTHA through Hardinge approach in femoral head avascular necrosis patients.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为临床结果研究，未涉及股骨近端应力/微动或有限元建模。
llm.why_not_core: No biomechanics modeling, no stress shielding or micromotion quantification, no FEA or implant-bone interface analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估一次双侧全髋关节置换术在股骨头坏死患者中的安全性和功能结果。
summary_zh.method: 前瞻性分析60例患者，采用Hardinge入路，记录并发症和改良Harris髋关节评分。
summary_zh.result: 无严重并发症，术后髋关节评分显著改善。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the safety and functional outcomes of one-stage bilateral total hip arthroplasty in patients with femoral head avascular necrosis.
summary_en.method: A prospective analysis of 60 patients undergoing one-stage bilateral THA via Hardinge approach, recording complications and modified Harris Hip Scores.
summary_en.result: No major complications occurred, and the hip scores improved significantly postoperatively.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up with serial radiographic and functional assessments.

papers.title: Inpatient rehabilitation for a patient following a total hip arthroplasty
papers.abstract: A patient, after receiving a total hip arthroplasty, was seen for physical therapy treatment for 8 sessions from 8/01/15 to 8/05/15 in an acute care hospital.Treatment was provided by a student physical therapist under the supervision of a licensed physical therapist.The patient was evaluated at the initial encounter with the Well's Clinical Prediction Rule to assess for the presence of deep vein thrombosis; the Numeric Pain Rating Scale was used to assess pain; the Physical Function ICU Test -Scored was used to assess strength; the Activity Measure for Post-Acute Care mobility short form was used to assess functional mobility; the 10 Meter Walk Test was used to assess gait speed; the Lower Extremity Function Scale was used to assess independence with ADL's; a plan of care was established based on the results of these outcome measures.Main goals for the patient were to improve pain, range of motion, strength, functional mobility, gait vi speed, and functional independence.Main interventions used were over-ground gait training, restorative training, resistive exercises, bed mobility and transfer training, and functional training.The patient improved in pain levels, strength, range of motion, functional mobility, gait speed, and functional independence.The patient was discharged to home with a home exercise program and a plan to follow-up with home health physical therapy.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为全髋关节置换术后康复的临床报告，未涉及任何生物力学建模或植入物力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical rehabilitation case study and does not include any biomechanical modeling, stress shielding analysis, micromotion quantification, or finite element simulation for hip implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 报告全髋关节置换术后患者的住院康复治疗过程。
summary_zh.method: 采用多种临床量表评估并实施物理治疗干预。
summary_zh.result: 患者在疼痛、力量、活动能力等方面均有改善。
summary_zh.validation: 单一病例的临床观察，无对照或量化力学验证。

summary_en.motivation: This case report documents the inpatient rehabilitation of a patient following total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: The patient underwent physical therapy including gait training, resistive exercises, and functional training, with outcomes measured by clinical scales.
summary_en.result: Improvements were observed in pain, strength, range of motion, functional mobility, and gait speed.
summary_en.validation: Validation is limited to a single patient case without biomechanical testing or quantitative mechanical analysis.
